questions.q: What is falah according to this lecture?
options: Success, from the word for farmer who plants and is patient
questions.explain: We plant and are patient, that is delayed gratification.

options: A charitable gift made permanent for public benefit
questions.explain: In Islamic civilisation, education and healthcare were funded by waqf.

questions.q: What do riba and yurbi share?
options: Both come from the root meaning to increase
questions.explain: Allah destroys riba and nurtures charity.

options: The ability to convey wide meaning in few words
questions.explain: Even the Prophet SAW had no words for the colours of Paradise.

questions.q: What is infaq according to this lecture?
options: Not only money, but energy, time and a listening ear
questions.explain: Lending an ear to people's problems is also infaq.

questions.q: What answered the Prophet's SAW sorrow at losing his son in Surah Al-Kawthar?
options: The gift of abundant good and that the hater is cut off
questions.explain: Quraysh greeted him with the slogan "Muhammad is cut off"; Allah revealed Al-Kawthar.

questions.q: What does Al-Ankabut 29:45 stress about prayer?
questions.explain: Prayer should leave a social impact.

questions.q: Why does minimalism fail according to the ustaz?
questions.explain: Beware consumerism that turns us into zombies.

questions.q: The ummah needs many talents across fields, not just doctors and engineers.
The sirah is only for remembering and weeping, not for reform.
questions.explain: False. The sirah is a story of reform, not nostalgia.

questions.q: Match each term with its meaning.

right.text: Delaying reward: planting and being patient
The natural disposition created by Allah
Economic thinking that turns education and healthcare into business
Spending wealth, energy or time in Allah's way

questions.explain: Infaq is spending wealth, energy and time, fitrah is natural disposition, neoliberalism turns education into business, and delayed gratification is delaying reward.

questions.q: We judge children only by exams. What does the ustaz advise?
options: Value diverse talents and create a good environment
questions.explain: Judging only by exams wastes talent.
